title: Oracle 11g, OFFLINE, converter_prereqs unanswered: urgency rises, the target does not change, the converter is unavailable, one schema gap, confidence stays medium

Contrast method-converter-prereqs-not-sure-unknown (a listed release), where it does.
adjudication: selected, inputs: the document selected a non-Microsoft converter. That converter is not a Microsoft product (OP-SCOPE), so the card carries the gap SCHEMA_CONVERSION. downtime changed from MINIMAL to OFFLINE (isolates the schema gap) and converter_prereqs from FOUNDRY_AND_COPILOT_READY to NOT_SURE (pins that an unselected converter does not make the field decision-driving).

title: Only flexible server survives: HorizonDB set aside by preview refusal, Oracle AI Database@Azure unsupported in koreacentral, so no alternative

No other family stands, so B2 names no alternative and says so; it does not name a product from another vendor.

derivation: pg_flex is primary. oracle_dbaz is eligible (swedencentral) and is the only other survivor, but the driver is ORACLE_LICENSE_COST: staying on Oracle keeps the licence cost the customer wants to leave, so B2 names no Oracle family as the alternative and the alternative is absent. oracle_vm is excluded by MANAGED_PAAS in any case.

title: OPEN_SOURCE_STRATEGY driver: Oracle AI Database@Azure survives but is not named as the alternative

derivation: Same profile as the licence-cost scenario with the driver OPEN_SOURCE_STRATEGY: an Oracle family is the opposite of an open-source strategy, so B2 names none and the alternative is absent although oracle_dbaz is eligible.

title: DATACENTER_EXIT driver: Oracle AI Database@Azure is the alternative when it is the only other survivor
why: B2: the Oracle families are legitimate alternatives for every driver except ORACLE_LICENSE_COST and OPEN_SOURCE_STRATEGY; the card states the winning condition.
derivation: pg_flex is primary. No other PostgreSQL family survives (horizondb excluded by PREVIEW_REFUSED, pg_vm and pg_aks by MANAGED_PAAS, pg_elastic held for its distribution key). oracle_dbaz is eligible, and DATACENTER_EXIT does not forbid an Oracle alternative, so it is the best-ranked other survivor: the alternative, which wins if the PostgreSQL rewrite is not funded or the application is certified only on Oracle. oracle_vm is excluded by MANAGED_PAAS.

title: REHOST_FIRST with NEAR_ZERO: an Oracle primary has no selected route and no ONLINE_CAPTURE gap

derivation: REHOST_FIRST ranks the stay-on-Oracle targets ahead of every PostgreSQL target; edition EE and oracle_dbaz survives (swedencentral), so it is the primary (OP-INTENT). The NEAR_ZERO downtime would carry the ONLINE_CAPTURE gap for a PostgreSQL target, but the move to Oracle is a rehost done with Oracle's own tooling, which this advisor does not cover: Step C does not apply, so no route is selected and no gap is raised. Confidence medium: every decision-driving field is answered.

B1 rule 1: REHOST_FIRST selects oracle_dbaz only when it survives and the topology or edition fits, otherwise oracle_vm; oracle_dbaz is not a survivor, so oracle_vm (eligible: SE2 on a single instance, no gate) is the primary, reported as OP-INTENT. 11g is below the converter range and NEAR_ZERO would need change capture, but Step C does not apply to an Oracle primary: no selected route, no SCHEMA_CONVERSION gap, no ONLINE_CAPTURE gap. Confidence medium. (Oracle 11g is in Sustaining Support: the card raises urgency and keeps the target.)

title: PREVIEW_REFUSED at 97 to 192 vCores with no management preference: flexible server and HorizonDB are set aside, PostgreSQL on VMs ranks first
why: OP-V6 PREVIEW_REFUSED, OP-COMPUTE (pg_vm and pg_aks eligible_with_remediation), OP-RANK maturity penalties 4 and 5.
derivation: Above 96 vCores flexible server is reachable only on the preview V6 SKUs, and PREVIEW_REFUSED sets it aside by preference (OP-V6); HorizonDB is set aside by the same refusal (OP-PREVIEW). OP-COMPUTE makes pg_vm and pg_aks eligible_with_remediation (large VM sizes exist; sizing is the operator's), and no management model is stated, so nothing excludes them. With no features the scores are the maturity penalties: pg_vm 4, pg_aks 5, so OP-RANK picks pg_vm and B2 names pg_aks. The elastic cluster keeps only its distribution-key hold, which is not a held better-ranked candidate (B3), so the status is provisional. MINIMAL above 1 TB is the online family (gap ONLINE_CAPTURE); confidence medium (management_model unanswered is recorded, not decision-driving).

title: REHOST_FIRST with an Oracle primary and a driver that bars an Oracle alternative: the alternative is the best-ranked PostgreSQL survivor (PostgreSQL on VMs, 4.5)
why: B2: the alternative is the best-ranked survivor of another family, ranked by OP-RANK, and an Oracle family is not named when the driver is ORACLE_LICENSE_COST.
derivation: REHOST_FIRST selects oracle_dbaz (EE, swedencentral in the list): OP-INTENT. The PostgreSQL targets keep their states: ADVANCED_QUEUING and JAVA_IN_DATABASE are redesign cells on pg_flex and workaround cells on pg_vm and pg_aks, and APP_LIMITED weighs a redesign at 3, so the scores are pg_flex 6, pg_vm 4.5 and pg_aks 5.5 (no management model is stated, so none is set aside; horizondb is excluded by PREVIEW_REFUSED and pg_elastic keeps its distribution-key hold). The driver is ORACLE_LICENSE_COST, so the other Oracle family (oracle_vm, eligible) is not named. B2 asks for the best-ranked survivor of another family, which is the lowest OP-RANK score among the PostgreSQL survivors: pg_vm (4.5), not the first PostgreSQL target in the list of families (pg_flex, 6). Step C does not apply to an Oracle primary: no gaps.
adjudication: alternative_target: decided from B2 ("the best-ranked survivor that is a different family from the primary"), which ranks by the OP-RANK score and not by the order of the family table.
